decisive_items: Biopsy of posterior left pleural thickening showed CD5+, CD10−, non-germinal center B-cell type
Avid irregular enhancement within the right cavernous sinus and enlargement of the right side compared with the left
response.rationale: The biopsy is diagnostic of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), and the cavernous sinus enhancement with cranial nerve palsies is consistent with lymphomatous infiltration. Systemic lymphadenopathy and pleural mass support a systemic lymphoma. Other candidates lack definitive tissue evidence or are contradicted by normal inflammatory markers or biopsy findings.

rejected.why: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome is an inflammatory condition but is a diagnosis of exclusion; the biopsy-proven B-cell lymphoma elsewhere makes lymphomatous involvement of the cavernous sinus more likely.
Sphenoid sinusitis does not explain the cavernous sinus enhancement, cranial nerve palsies, or systemic lymphadenopathy and pleural mass.
Giant cell arteritis is unlikely given normal ESR and CRP, and the absence of typical features like jaw claudication or vision loss.
Sarcoidosis could cause lymphadenopathy and cavernous sinus involvement, but the biopsy shows B-cell lymphoma, not non-caseating granulomas.
Metastatic prostate cancer is not supported by the biopsy, which shows B-cell lymphoma, and the systemic pattern is more consistent with lymphoma.
